name: NHIL
description: National Health Insurance Levy — 2.5% of the taxable value. Claimable as input tax on purchases (Act 1151).

name: GETFund Levy
description: Ghana Education Trust Fund Levy — 2.5% of the same taxable value as NHIL and VAT. Claimable as input tax on purchases (Act 1151).

name: VAT (Standard Rate)
description: VAT 15% of the same taxable value as NHIL and GETFund. Not calculated on top of those levies (Act 1151).

name: Tourism Levy
description: Tourism Development Levy (L.I. 2185) — separate from VAT base

name: Withholding Tax (Goods)
description: Resident WHT on supply of goods exceeding the GRA invoice threshold — 2026 rate

name: Withholding Tax (Works)
description: Resident WHT on works/contracts (e.g. construction, building works) — 2026 rate

name: Withholding Tax (Rent — commercial)
description: Resident WHT on rent of non-residential business premises — 15%. Final tax. Residential rent is the separate 8% rule.

name: Withholding Tax (Rent — residential)
description: Resident WHT on rent of residential premises — 8%. Final tax.

name: PAYE (Income Tax)
description: Progressive monthly PAYE on taxable income — Act 1178 resident bands, effective 1 Sep 2026 (first GHS 588 at 0%, 35% above GHS 50,000). Each tier is the width of that slice; edit the tiers if GRA revises the bands. The last tier (rate 35, no upto) is open-ended.

name: Tier 1
description: Mandatory basic national pension, remitted to SSNIT: 13.5% of BASIC SALARY only (5.5% employee, 8% employer) — allowances, bonuses, and overtime are excluded from the base. Capped at the monthly insurable-earnings ceiling, floored at the minimum insurable earnings. Rename this rule to match how you refer to it on payslips (e.g. "SSNIT") — the rename is purely cosmetic and does not change the calculation. VERIFY the current rate/ceiling/floor against SSNIT guidance before relying on this for a real payroll run.

name: Tier 2
description: Mandatory occupational pension, remitted to a licensed private trustee (separate institution from Tier 1/SSNIT): 5% of BASIC SALARY, employer-funded only — no employee deduction. Same base rules as Tier 1 (basic salary only, capped/floored at the insurable-earnings limits). Rename this rule to your actual trustee's name — cosmetic only. VERIFY the current rate against your trustee/NPRA guidance before relying on this for a real payroll run.

name: Tier 3
description: Voluntary provident fund, remitted to a private trustee of the employee's choosing — a separate institution from Tier 1 and Tier 2. Not itself a withholding: this rule stores the tax-relief ceiling (% of basic salary) for how much of the employee's elected contribution is tax-relieved; the elected contribution rate lives on the employee record (Employee.tier3ContributionPct), since it's chosen per employee, not statutory. Rename this rule to your provident fund provider's name — cosmetic only. VERIFY current NPRA guidance before relying on this for a real payroll run.
